title: Compliance Reporting Pack v1 (Retention Controls + Audit Logging) — Outline & Generation
author: Daniel Carter
body:
## Purpose
This page defines the **baseline Compliance Reporting Pack (v1)** that Redwood Inference provides to enterprise prospects/customers to reduce security review friction and to support SOC 2 / ISO 27001-aligned evidence collection.

This is **not** a certification. It is a curated, repeatable set of summaries and evidence pointers that explain Redwood’s retention controls and audit logging posture, plus the operational proof points we can provide.

## Intended audiences
**Primary (customer/prospect):**
- Security / GRC teams (control owners, auditors, risk assessors)
- Platform/security engineering (implementation validation)

**Secondary (customer/prospect):**
- Procurement / vendor risk management (VRM)
- Legal (data handling, retention, legal hold expectations)

**Internal:**
- Sales/Solutions Engineering (standard, consistent artifacts)
- Support/Success (consistent answers and escalation path)

## What is included (v1)
The pack is structured as two deliverables:
1) **Customer-facing PDF** (shareable under NDA) with Redwood’s posture and scoped statements.
2) **Evidence bundle (ZIP)** (restricted; shared only when appropriate) with selected screenshots, configuration snapshots, and sample exports.

### Artifact list and cadence
| Artifact | Format | Audience | Source of truth | Owner | Refresh cadence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Compliance Reporting Pack (v1) — Summary | PDF | Customer Security/GRC, Procurement | This outline + generator inputs | GRC (Olga Petrov) | Quarterly + on material change |
| Control-to-Evidence Matrix (Retention + Audit Logging) | Table (PDF appendix + CSV in ZIP) | Customer Security/GRC | Confluence control mapping page | GRC (Olga Petrov) | Quarterly |
| Retention Controls Overview (what’s configurable; defaults; guardrails) | PDF section | Customer Security/Eng | Confluence retention overview page | Product (Naomi Feldman) | On product change |
| Audit Logging Coverage Summary | PDF section | Customer Security/Eng | Audit logging Confluence page | Security Eng (Marcus Lin) | On product change |
| Retention Policy Attestation (how policy is evaluated; enforcement evidence types) | PDF section + ZIP evidence | Customer Security/GRC | Policy schema + enforcement docs | Platform Eng (Ethan Park) | Quarterly |
| Evidence Collection Procedure (internal) | Confluence page link (not customer-facing by default) | Internal | Evidence runbook | GRC (Olga Petrov) | Quarterly |

## Scope and boundaries (v1)
### In scope
- Tenant-configurable retention controls for the datasets explicitly supported in v1 (see “Data types covered”)
- Audit log retention behavior and export boundaries
- Legal hold semantics and exception process (high-level, non-sensitive)
- Evidence types demonstrating enforcement and auditability (policy snapshots, job run records, sample exports)

### Out of scope (v1)
- Customer-configurable retention for every internal infrastructure log stream (some are governed by SRE/vendor constraints)
- Customer-configurable retention for all raw inference payload content (where not supported/eligible)
- Full SOC 2 report distribution (handled separately under NDA and governed by Legal)

## Pack structure (recommended PDF outline)
### 1. Executive summary (1–2 pages)
- What Redwood Inference is (Hosted API / Dedicated / Private)
- What this pack covers (retention controls + audit logging) and what it does not
- High-level statements:
  - Retention policies are **configurable per tenant** within guardrails
  - Retention enforcement is **automated**, monitored, and auditable
  - Audit logs are **exportable** and exports respect retention boundaries

### 2. Product and deployment context
- Deployment modes: Hosted / Dedicated / Private
- Shared concepts:
  - Tenant identity
  - Regions/environments
  - Control plane vs data plane
- What varies by deployment mode (at a high level)

### 3. Data types covered (v1)
List the datasets for which v1 supports tenant-configurable retention and/or provides enforceable retention behavior.

**Covered categories (v1):**
- Audit logs (security-relevant events)
- Admin activity (Console/API configuration changes)
- Inference request metadata (non-payload metadata where applicable/eligible)
- Telemetry/analytics tables explicitly designated as eligible
- Operational logs *where applicable* and within platform constraints

**For each category, include:**
- What it contains (plain-language)
- Why it exists (security/operations/billing)
- Default retention by product tier (Hosted/Dedicated/Private, where applicable)
- Configurable range (min/max) and guardrails
- Legal hold behavior

### 4. Retention policy model and guardrails (customer-facing)
- Policy hierarchy and precedence (conceptual):
  - Tenant-level policy
  - Environment/region overrides (where supported)
  - System guardrails
- Guardrails (examples to include):
  - Minimum retention for audit logs and admin activity
  - Maximum retention limits (for operational scalability)
  - “Never delete” is disallowed unless explicitly permitted under enterprise agreement and technical feasibility
- Legal hold:
  - What legal hold means in the platform
  - What datasets are impacted
  - How holds prevent deletion while active

### 5. Enforcement approach and auditability
Explain how Redwood enforces retention and how we prove it.

Include:
- Storage-level TTL where supported
- Scheduled deletion/compaction jobs where TTL is insufficient
- Idempotency and safety controls (batch size limits, rate limits)
- Monitoring and alerting (lag/backlog, error rate, storage growth signals)
- What “proof” looks like:
  - Effective policy snapshot (before/after)
  - Enforcement job run history (timestamps, volume deleted, failures)
  - Data sampling/verification steps (internal)

### 6. Audit logging coverage and exports
- What is logged (categories of security-relevant events)
- Who can access audit logs (RBAC summary)
- Export formats (e.g., JSONL/CSV) and delivery methods
- Retention interaction:
  - Exports cannot retrieve data older than retention windows
  - Export metadata includes retention boundary notes/warnings
- Private deployment considerations (where applicable):
  - Customer-managed storage or SIEM routing options (if enabled)

### 7. Operational processes (high-level)
Provide process statements that a customer’s GRC team expects, without exposing sensitive internal-only details.
- Retention exceptions and legal holds workflow (request, approval, documentation, review cadence)
- Change management summary (how retention policy changes are audited)
- Incident response linkage (audit logs and retention evidence support investigations)

### 8. Control-to-evidence mapping (appendix)
- Include a short narrative: how to read the matrix
- Include the matrix itself (SOC 2 / ISO-style framing)
- Clearly label which evidence is included in the ZIP vs available upon request

### 9. Appendix: Definitions and glossary
- Tenant, environment, region
- Retention window, enforcement, legal hold
- Audit log vs operational logs
- “Inference request metadata” vs payload

## Evidence bundle (ZIP) contents (restricted)
Recommended structure for a standardized ZIP:
- /00-readme.pdf (what’s included, how it was generated, date/time)
- /01-policy-snapshots/
  - effective-policy-<tenant>-<env>-<date>.json (sanitized)
- /02-enforcement-evidence/
  - enforcement-job-summary-<date>.csv
  - screenshots (Console effective policy + last enforcement run) if allowed
- /03-audit-logging/
  - sample-audit-export-<date>.jsonl (sanitized)
  - export-metadata-<date>.txt
- /04-control-matrix/
  - control-mapping-retention-audit-logging-<date>.csv

**Sanitization requirements:**
- No customer identifiers beyond the intended recipient tenant (if customer-specific)
- No secrets, tokens, internal hostnames, or raw payload content
- Use redaction for user emails where possible; retain role names and event types

## Update cadence and triggers
**Standard cadence:** quarterly refresh for the PDF narrative and control mapping.

**Material-change triggers (out-of-band refresh):**
- Changes to retention defaults or guardrail ranges
- New dataset added to “eligible for customer-configurable retention” list
- Audit logging schema changes that affect coverage claims
- New export limitations or behavior changes
- Enforcement mechanism changes (e.g., TTL → deletion worker or vice versa)

## How to generate the pack (internal procedure)
> Note: The actual generator implementation details live in the internal runbook and tooling ticket trail. This section describes the expected workflow at a high level.

### Preconditions
- Confirm the request context (prospect vs existing customer; Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
- Confirm NDA status and sharing restrictions
- Determine whether the output is:
  - “Generic Redwood” pack (no customer identifiers)
  - Customer-specific pack (includes tenant configuration snapshots)

### Inputs
- Current retention controls overview (Confluence)
- Control-to-evidence mapping (Confluence)
- Audit log retention and export behavior (Confluence)
- Latest product defaults and supported datasets list (from data inventory source)
- Optional: customer tenant effective policy snapshot (if customer-specific)

### Generation steps (repeatable)
1) Pull latest narrative sections from Confluence source pages.
2) Generate or export the current control-to-evidence matrix.
3) Collect evidence artifacts as permitted (policy snapshots, enforcement summaries, sample exports).
4) Run the compliance pack generator to assemble:
   - Customer-facing PDF
   - Evidence ZIP
5) Perform QA checks (see below).
6) Obtain approvals.
7) Distribute via approved secure channel (Sales/SE workflow).

### QA checklist (minimum)
- PDF has correct version/date, and correct deployment mode scope (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)
- All statements match current product behavior and documented guardrails
- Any screenshots are current and do not expose restricted internals
- Evidence ZIP contains no secrets and has consistent filenames
- Retention boundaries are consistent across:
  - narrative defaults
  - policy snapshot evidence
  - export behavior description

### Approvals and sign-off
- GRC owner: Olga Petrov (required)
- Security Engineering: Marcus Lin (required for audit logging statements)
- Product Security & Compliance: Naomi Feldman (required for externally-facing claims/positioning)
- Legal (as needed): Michael Grant / Sofia Mendes for customer-specific language or legal hold terms

### Distribution guidance
- Customer-facing PDF: shareable under NDA via Sales/Solutions Engineering approved channel
- Evidence ZIP: share only when explicitly requested and approved (restricted)
- Always watermark customer-facing PDFs with:
  - “Confidential — Provided under NDA”
  - Generated date
  - Recipient company name (if customer-specific)
